title: KV Compaction: Metrics + Dashboard Requirements (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
content:
Goal / audience
- Audience: SRE oncall + runtime oncall (primary), perf/benchmarking (secondary), product (read-only)
- Goal: single dashboard that answers: (1) are tail lat spikes correlated with compaction/eviction? (2) are we fragmented and trending worse? (3) is compaction doing “reasonable” work within budget? (4) are we evicting too aggressively / impacting customer sessions? (5) can we safely roll forward/back / flip kill switch?
- Assumes compaction/eviction are gated behind feature flags and configured by tier/model/profile.

Scope of this document
- Required metrics (names + labels/breakdowns) that must exist in telemetry.
- Dashboard layout: panels, recommended queries, and drill-down workflows.
- Trace exemplars: required span names/tags and how to link from metrics to traces.
- NOT defining alert thresholds here (see guardrails / rollout policy). We DO call out which panels must support alerting.

Reference / related
- KV compaction project: runtime-1.22
- Primary tickets: ENG-4822 (metrics), ENG-4830 (dashboards)
- Tracing PR: redwood/pr-19405
- Kill switch + config plumbing: redwood/pr-19422

Naming notes
- We should follow the existing runtime metrics prefix patterns (runtime_kv_*). If the telemetry platform requires different casing or prefixes, keep a mapping in the dashboard description.
- All counters should be monotonic counters; rates computed in dashboard.
- All gauges should be exported per runtime instance, aggregated by pool/cluster.


REQUIRED METRICS (must-have)

A) Fragmentation + allocator health (core)
1) runtime_kv_arena_fragmentation_ratio (gauge, 0..1)
- Definition: 1 - (largest_contiguous_free_bytes / total_free_bytes) OR agreed allocator definition (must be documented in metric help text).
- Labels required:
  - model_id (or model_family + variant)
  - pool (hosted / dedicated / private)
  - tier (hosted-free/hosted-paid/enterprise, etc. if applicable)
  - region
  - gpu_type (A100/H100/L4 etc.)
  - kv_profile (quantization/layout profile if exposed internally)
- Labels optional but strongly preferred:
  - allocator_version (to correlate changes)
  - runtime_build

2) runtime_kv_arena_free_bytes (gauge)
3) runtime_kv_arena_used_bytes (gauge)
4) runtime_kv_arena_total_bytes (gauge)
- These three are required for basic “capacity vs fragmentation” context.
- Same labels as above.

5) runtime_kv_arena_largest_free_block_bytes (gauge)
- Used to debug “we have free bytes but can’t fit requests” situations.

6) runtime_kv_allocation_failures_total (counter)
- Increment on allocation failure that would have succeeded with perfect contiguity (if we can distinguish), otherwise count all allocator failures with reason label.
- Required label: reason (oom / fragmented / limit / unknown)

7) runtime_kv_arena_defrag_time_ms_total (counter)
- If we still have any implicit defrag/slow-path, must be measured separately from compaction.

B) Compaction work + budget + overhead
8) runtime_kv_compaction_enabled (gauge: 0/1)
- Labels: model_id, pool, region, kv_profile.

9) runtime_kv_compaction_runs_total (counter)
- Increment once per compaction “cycle” (however defined: scheduler step, background pass, etc.).
- Required label: trigger (threshold / alloc_fail / periodic / manual / scheduler_phase)

10) runtime_kv_compaction_bytes_moved_total (counter)
- Required label: move_type (page_move / block_move / pack / copy)

11) runtime_kv_compaction_time_ms_total (counter)
- Required label: phase (scan / select / copy / remap / verify / commit)
- Minimum requirement: overall compaction time; phases preferred.

12) runtime_kv_compaction_budget_bytes (gauge)
13) runtime_kv_compaction_budget_time_ms (gauge)
- Required label: enforcement_point (scheduler / background)
- These are the configured budgets currently active (not “consumed”).

14) runtime_kv_compaction_budget_bytes_consumed_total (counter)
15) runtime_kv_compaction_budget_time_ms_consumed_total (counter)
- Labels: enforcement_point, scheduler_phase (prefill_boundary / decode_boundary / idle)

16) runtime_kv_compaction_stops_total (counter)
- Required label: reason (budget_exhausted / no_candidates / safety_invariant / lock_contention / cancelled_req / disabled)

17) runtime_kv_compaction_errors_total (counter)
- Required label: error_type (relocation_failed / map_inconsistent / verify_failed / timeout / unknown)
- This should be near-zero; any increase is page-worthy.

C) Eviction behavior + impact
18) runtime_kv_evictions_total (counter)
- Required labels:
  - eviction_reason (oom_prevent / fragmentation / tier_policy / max_sessions / manual)
  - victim_type (sequence / prefix_cache / other)
  - tier_victim (paid/dedicated/etc. if applicable)

19) runtime_kv_evicted_bytes_total (counter)
- Same labels as evictions_total.

20) runtime_kv_eviction_selection_time_ms_total (counter)
- Helps identify eviction scanning overhead.

21) runtime_kv_eviction_denied_total (counter)
- Required label: reason (pinned / min_residency / in_flight_relocation / policy_block)

22) runtime_kv_active_sequences (gauge)
23) runtime_kv_pinned_sequences (gauge)
- Necessary to understand when eviction pressure is expected and when policy is too aggressive.

D) Latency correlation signals (minimum set)
24) request_decode_latency_ms (histogram) AND request_end_to_end_latency_ms (histogram)
- Must be sliceable by model_id/pool/region/tier.
- We need at least p50/p95/p99 views.

25) runtime_scheduler_tick_time_ms (histogram or summary)
- To catch compaction causing long scheduler ticks.

26) runtime_kv_overload_backpressure_events_total (counter)
- Required label: action (reject / queue / shed / reroute)
- Used to correlate “compaction fixed OOM but increased shedding” scenarios.


STRONGLY RECOMMENDED METRICS (nice-to-have but should land before broad rollout)
- runtime_kv_arena_fragmentation_ratio_by_shard (gauge) if allocator is sharded; label shard_id.
- runtime_kv_compaction_candidate_pages (gauge) and runtime_kv_compaction_candidate_bytes (gauge)
- runtime_kv_compaction_lock_wait_ms_total (counter) and lock_contention_events_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_eviction_lru_scan_count_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate (gauge or derived) with “eviction victim_type=prefix_cache” breakdown
- runtime_kv_relocation_cancel_race_total (counter) (post pr-19440 lessons)


DASHBOARD LAYOUT (what panels we need)

Dashboard name
- “Runtime / KV Cache: Fragmentation + Compaction + Eviction (runtime-1.22)”

Global filters (top of dashboard)
- Time range (default 6h; quick picks 30m/6h/24h/7d)
- pool (hosted/dedicated/private)
- region
- model_id (or model family)
- tier
- gpu_type
- kv_profile
- build / allocator_version (if available)

Section 0: Rollout + safety (top row; must support oncall)
Panel 0.1: Compaction enabled (% of instances)
- Query: avg(runtime_kv_compaction_enabled) by (pool, region, model_id)
- Purpose: confirm rollout cohort

Panel 0.2: Kill-switch / config freshness (if we have it)
- If a “config_version” or “flag_last_update_age_sec” exists, show it.
- Otherwise: add a markdown panel linking to the runbook steps for verifying flags on an instance.

Panel 0.3: Allocation failures rate
- Query: rate(runtime_kv_allocation_failures_total[5m]) by (reason)
- Purpose: immediate severity signal

Panel 0.4: Compaction errors rate
- Query: rate(runtime_kv_compaction_errors_total[5m]) by (error_type)

Section 1: Fragmentation overview (fast diagnosis)
Panel 1.1: Fragmentation ratio over time (p50/p90/p99 across instances)
- Aggregation: quantiles across instances within filter scope.
- Must show p99 because fragmentation is often “one bad node causes tail”.

Panel 1.2: Largest free block bytes vs total free bytes
- Two lines; helps identify “free but not contiguous”.

Panel 1.3: Capacity gauges (used/free/total)
- Stacked area is preferred (used + free = total).

Panel 1.4: Fragmentation heatmap by node (or shard)
- If the platform supports: top N worst instances by fragmentation_ratio.
- Must include click-through to instance-level view.

Section 2: Compaction activity + budget compliance
Panel 2.1: Compaction bytes moved (rate)
- Query: rate(runtime_kv_compaction_bytes_moved_total[5m]) by (move_type)

Panel 2.2: Compaction time (rate) and “bytes per ms” efficiency
- Two panels or one panel with derived series:
  - rate(time_ms_total) and rate(bytes_moved_total)
  - bytes_per_ms = rate(bytes)/rate(ms)
- Purpose: detect expensive compactions (low efficiency) correlating with latency spikes.

Panel 2.3: Budget consumed vs budget configured
- Derived: consumed_time_ms_per_min, consumed_bytes_per_min, plus overlay of configured budgets.
- Breakdowns: enforcement_point + scheduler_phase.

Panel 2.4: Compaction stop reasons
- Query: rate(runtime_kv_compaction_stops_total[10m]) by (reason)
- “budget_exhausted” should be common; “safety_invariant” and “lock_contention” should be rare.

Panel 2.5: Before/after impact view (fragmentation ratio vs compaction runs)
- Dual-axis: fragmentation ratio and compaction_runs rate.
- Goal: see if compaction is actually reducing fragmentation.

Section 3: Eviction behavior + customer impact proxies
Panel 3.1: Evictions rate (by reason, victim_type)
- Query: rate(runtime_kv_evictions_total[5m]) by (eviction_reason, victim_type)

Panel 3.2: Evicted bytes rate
- Query: rate(runtime_kv_evicted_bytes_total[5m]) by (eviction_reason)

Panel 3.3: Eviction denied rate (pinned/min-residency)
- Query: rate(runtime_kv_eviction_denied_total[10m]) by (reason)

Panel 3.4: Active sequences + pinned sequences
- Two time series.
- Helps interpret high eviction: is it legitimate pressure or policy misbehavior.

Panel 3.5 (optional if metric exists): Prefix cache hit rate + prefix-cache eviction rate
- Goal: ensure eviction doesn’t destroy caching economics silently.

Section 4: Latency correlation (the “so what” section)
Panel 4.1: Request latency p95/p99 (end-to-end)
- Query: p95/p99 from request_end_to_end_latency_ms histogram.
- Must support breakdown by model_id and tier.

Panel 4.2: Decode latency p95/p99
- Same but decode-focused.

Panel 4.3: Scheduler tick time p99
- Watch for compaction introducing long ticks.

Panel 4.4: Correlation panel (overlay)
- On same graph (or aligned panels):
  - request p99
  - compaction bytes moved rate
  - eviction rate
  - fragmentation ratio p99
- Goal: enable quick “compaction caused latency?” vs “compaction mitigated pressure?” read.

Panel 4.5: Backpressure / shedding / reroute events
- Query: rate(runtime_kv_overload_backpressure_events_total[5m]) by (action)
- Rollout guardrail input.

Section 5: Drilldowns (links / saved views)
- Link to “Top N worst instances by fragmentation ratio (last 30m)”
- Link to “Compaction-heavy instances (bytes moved top N)”
- Link to “Eviction-heavy instances (evictions top N) broken down by tier_victim”


TRACE EXEMPLARS (required for debugging)

We need trace-to-metrics linking so an oncaller can jump from a latency spike to compaction activity on the same instance.

Required spans
1) Span: runtime.kv.compaction
- Tags:
  - model_id
  - pool
  - region
  - kv_profile
  - trigger
  - bytes_moved
  - pages_moved (if available)
  - time_ms
  - enforcement_point
  - scheduler_phase
  - stop_reason (if any)
  - error_type (if error)

2) Span: runtime.kv.evict
- Tags:
  - eviction_reason
  - victim_type
  - evicted_bytes
  - tier_victim
  - selection_time_ms

3) Span (optional but recommended): runtime.kv.relocate_page / runtime.kv.remap
- Used for deep dives (lock contention, cancellation hazards).

Exemplar requirements
- request latency histograms should store exemplars that include trace_id.
- We should emit exemplars preferentially when:
  - compaction occurs in same window as a request
  - eviction occurs
  - scheduler tick time is above a threshold

Trace search “canned queries” to include as dashboard links
- “Find traces where runtime.kv.compaction bytes_moved > X and request latency p99 elevated”
- “Find traces with runtime.kv.evict eviction_reason=oom_prevent”
- “Find traces with compaction error_type != none”


BREAKDOWNS / CARDINALITY GUARDRAILS
- model_id can be high-cardinality. If needed, use model_family + model_variant (curated set) for global panels; keep full model_id only in filtered drilldowns.
- instance_id label should NOT be on every metric by default. Prefer:
  - global aggregate metrics without instance_id
  - separate “*_by_instance” metrics OR rely on infra label injection only for selected metrics that need top-N (fragmentation_ratio, allocation_failures_total, compaction_errors_total).
- tier labels must be stable and limited (e.g., hosted_free/hosted_pro/enterprise/dedicated/private).


MINIMUM DASHBOARD ACCEPTANCE (what ‘done’ means)
- A new dashboard exists with the above sections 0–4.
- For Hosted + Dedicated pools, filters work and panels render within acceptable query time.
- We can answer these oncall questions in <5 minutes:
  1) Is compaction enabled for this pool/model/region?
  2) Are we fragmented (and on how many nodes)?
  3) Is compaction doing work within configured budget?
  4) Are we evicting (and which tiers are being hit)?
  5) Did p99 move in the same window as compaction/eviction/backpressure?


OPEN QUESTIONS / TODO
- Confirm final definition of fragmentation_ratio with Omar/Samir (largest free block vs other heuristic). Update metric help text and this doc accordingly.
- Decide whether “allocation_failures_total reason=fragmented” can be reliably detected.
- Telemetry platform: validate exemplar support on request histograms for Hosted API traffic.
- Determine whether we should add a lightweight “config_version” gauge for flag propagation debugging (requested by platform team thread).

Changelog
- 2026-01-16: Initial draft from SRE + runtime sync; included must-have metrics + initial dashboard sections.
- 2026-01-28: Added budget consumed metrics and trace tag requirements after scheduler integration review.
- 2026-02-11: Updated eviction breakdowns to include tier_victim and victim_type; added cardinality guardrails.
